# The sequence #381 and #382 came out of: scaffold a workflow, then point the
# rest of the tool at what the scaffold wrote. Each of these is somebody's first
# five minutes with `flow`, and the failure they cover is a template that has
# drifted past the grammar — which nothing compiles, so only a walk like this
# one can see it.
$ flow init demo
-- exit --
0
-- stderr --
# The formatter has to accept its own tool's output, with nothing left to do —
# and to say so about the test file beside it rather than rewriting it.
$ flow fmt demo
-- exit --
0
-- stdout --
demo/workflow.test.yaml: test file; flow fmt does not format test files
demo/workflow.yaml: already formatted

# Twice, which is the idempotence a pre-commit hook needs.
$ flow fmt demo
-- exit --
0
-- stdout --
demo/workflow.test.yaml: test file; flow fmt does not format test files
demo/workflow.yaml: already formatted

# The grammar accepts it, which is what a template that has drifted would fail.
$ flow validate demo
-- exit --
0

# The scaffold's own case passes, so the workflow and the test file beside it
# agree about step ids and the task's inputs.
$ flow test demo
-- exit --
0

# And it is already in the edition this build speaks, which is the assertion
# that goes red on the day the edition moves and the template does not.
$ flow fix --check demo/workflow.yaml
-- exit --
0
-- stdout --
demo/workflow.yaml: already current
